topics: Dedicated vs hosted routing and pricing
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-26 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Aurora Partnerships), Priya Sharma (VP Cloud), Ethan Liu (Solutions Architect)
---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick round robin?
[00:12] Carlos (Aurora): thanks maya, carlos here, partnerships at Aurora. priya and ethan are with me.
[00:18] Priya (Aurora): hi all, priya - vp cloud, excited to learn more about redwood and see how we can partner.
[00:24] Liam (Redwood-SE): hey, liam here - i'll focus on the technical side. we usually pair on AE conversations.
[00:30] Maya: cool, agenda - quick intros, goals from aurora, high-level redwood overview, integration patterns, security/questions, and next steps. sound good?
[00:40] Carlos: yep, good. our motivations: we want to offer customers a turnkey LLM inference integration on aurora infra - think marketplace images or a managed peering option. we also want to show perf numbers on our H100 and next-gen racks.
[00:55] Maya: awesome - main ways we partner: marketplace AMI/container + turnkey hops, or private deployment where redwood control plane talks to customer-managed nodes, or dedicated peering for large accounts. each has different ops/security tradeoffs.
[01:12] Ethan (Aurora): curious about the private deployment model - does redwood ship a control plane that sits in our VPC? any on-prem airgap option?
[01:22] Liam: yes. we have three patterns: hosted api (fastest, redwood-hosted), dedicated/reserved capacity (redwood-managed infra with isolation), and private deployment (control plane optionally hosted, runtime runs in customer VPC or on-prem). for private we deliver deployment artifacts - container images and k8s helm charts for an on-prem runtime. we also support VPC peering and SSO for control plane access.
[01:45] Priya: ok that's promising. security is big for enterprise customers - SOC2, ISO, audit logs, KMS integration. what does redwood offer here?
[01:55] Maya: we have SOC2 reports, support for customer-managed KMS/HSM, encryption in transit and at rest, audit logs surfaced in console, RBAC/SSO via SAML. i'll follow up with the SOC2 snapshot and the KMS integration guide.
[02:12] Carlos: do you have documentation for VPC peering and firewall rules? some of our customers require very specific egress whitelisting.
[02:20] Liam: yes - we have a private deployment networking guide and a list of ports/IPs; i'll attach that. note: for fully air-gapped we provide an on-prem bundle but that's a longer sales path.
[02:35] Priya: great. on the perf side - what kind of models and latency targets are realistic on your runtime?
[02:42] Liam: depends on model size and quantization. for a trimmed 13B quantized to 4bit on H100 we typically see X tokens/sec at p95 latency ~200ms for single-turn generative workloads, batching and prefix caching change the numbers. we can run a benchmark on aurora's H100 cluster to get concrete numbers.
[03:05] Carlos: can you explain prefix caching? sometimes the term gets confused across teams.
[03:12] Liam: sure - prefix or KV cache stores previous activations so repeated context reuse (long chats, system prompts) doesn't recompute. reduces per-token compute when you have many similar prompts. sorry sometimes the auto transcriber calls it 'KV cash' in our notes...
[03:28] Maya: hah, yes we've seen 'KV cash' appear before.
[03:33] Ethan: on the benchmark - what do you need from our side?
[03:38] Liam: ideally: a short-lived account or a test env on your cluster with a couple of nodes (H100/ A100), a sample prompt set representative of your customers, and networking access so our runner can push jobs. we can run model variants (7B, 13B quantized, 70B float) to show tradeoffs.
[03:56] Carlos: we can provide a small tenant and ssh/creds for a sandbox. i'll check with ops.
[04:02] Priya: licensing/questions around bringing models - do you require model artifacts to leave customer environment? some customers want models to stay in their VPC.
[04:12] Maya: private deployment keeps model artifacts in-customer. hosted api obviously uses redwood infra; dedicated can be redwood-managed but with contractual data isolation. will include options in the doc.
[04:24] Carlos: great. what about billing and pricing integration - marketplace vs reseller?
[04:31] Maya: marketplace AMI/container is easiest for GTM - customers bring their own redwood account and we bill usage. for joint enterprise deals we do reserved capacity and can partner on co-sell/reseller pricing.
[04:43] Ethan: we occasionally see customers who want SSO and audit trail integrated into their enterprise SIEM - how exportable are your logs?
[04:51] Liam: logs and traces can be exported to S3 or to a customer SIEM via webhook/forwarder; we also have token-level cost breakdowns in the console.
[05:02] Carlos: any compliance blockers we should know about for EU data residency?
[05:09] Maya: we have EU regions for hosted but for strict residency customers private deployments in-region/on-prem is the recommended route.
[05:18] Priya: ok good. switching to integration work - are there sample images or terraform modules for provisioning?
[05:26] Liam: yes - we provide container images and terraform modules for cluster resources; for k8s we have helm charts and an operator. we'll share a repo link.
[05:35] Carlos: nice. some of our platform customers want inference endpoints as a managed service in our marketplace - can we white-label or embed redwood endpoints?
[05:44] Maya: our marketplace approach supports partner listing and easy onboarding; white-labeling requires a bit more legal/brand work but is doable for larger partners.
[05:53] Ethan: for the benchmark, any recommended prompt set? we can coordinate but curious if redwood has standard evals.
[06:00] Liam: we have standard eval sets and we'll also ask you for a few custom prompts representative of your customers. the benchmark plan will include throughput/latency/cost per token and quality checks.
[06:15] Carlos: competitors question - our sales team will ask how this compares to Lambda Labs or replicate. what are the key differentiators?
[06:23] Maya: redwood focuses on production inference controls - predictable latency, routing policies, caching, and observability. unlike some competitors, we provide unified tooling for hosted, dedicated, and private so customers can migrate without refactoring.
[06:38] Priya: one technical question - what's the recommended networking topology for minimal latency?
[06:44] Liam: colocating runtime in the same VPC/region is ideal. for peered setups we recommend direct peering and low-latency interconnects; avoid cross-region requests for latency-sensitive endpoints.
[06:58] Carlos: any special kernel or driver requirements on aurora hosts?
[07:03] Liam: runtime is tuned for modern nvidia stacks (cuda 12+, cuDNN/ libs we list). we also have profiles for custom kernels but will need your infra team to confirm driver versions.
[07:16] Priya: ok. can we talk about support model - sla and pager?
[07:22] Maya: for dedicated we include SLAs and 24/7 support tiers; private deployments have an enterprise support contract option. we'll surface specifics in partner docs.
[07:33] Ethan: curious about multi-tenant security - if we run redwood runtime on our infra, how are tenants isolated?
[07:40] Liam: we recommend namespace-level isolation with network policies and optional model sandboxing. data encryption per-tenant is supported if you provide KMS keys.
[07:52] Carlos: this is great. switching to commercial - what are typical committed sizes for dedicated?
[07:59] Maya: starts as small as a few reserved GPUs monthly for early customers; enterprise customers commit at rack scale with discounts. pricing depends on GPU class and guarantee levels.
[08:10] Priya: any quick wins we can show to customers in 30 days?
[08:15] Maya: yes - a marketplace listing with a 1-click AMI and a short benchmark report is often a 30-day deliverable.
[08:22] Carlos: let's aim for that.
[08:25] Liam: for the benchmark plan i'll include the exact workloads, data transfer plan, and cost estimate.
[08:32] Maya: ok, can we capture a few integration risks? network egress and firewall rules, driver mismatches, model licensing for 3rd-party model artifacts, and customer expectation on latency.
[08:45] Priya: model licensing is big - some customers want to bring their own models with commercial licenses.
[08:50] Liam: we can support BYO models; we'll note the license checklist.
[08:56] Carlos: any redwood SDK requirements? our devs prefer python and rest endpoints.
[09:02] Maya: we have python and js sdks, and a simple rest api. sample code in the partner repo.
[09:09] Ethan: will there be any agent or sidecar that needs to run on the host?
[09:13] Liam: a small runtime container is required for model serving; we can run as a sidecar or as a node service depending on topology.
[09:20] Carlos: what about metrics - prometheus/exporter?
[09:24] Liam: we support prometheus metrics and traces; you can scrape or forward.
[09:29] Maya: ok i want to confirm owners and next steps - i'll send partner deck + SOC2 summary, liam will draft benchmark spec, carlos will coordinate access to a sandbox cluster, and priya will loop in GTM contacts. agreed?
[09:45] Priya: agreed.
[09:47] Carlos: agreed, will check on ops side for access.
[09:52] Maya: perfect. any final questions?
[09:56] Ethan: just one - sample timeline for demo?
[10:00] Maya: if we get sandbox access this week, liam can run a quick smoke test in ~3 business days, full perf run in 7-10 days.
[10:10] Priya: ok sounds reasonable.
[10:13] Maya: thanks all. we'll follow up with notes and the artifacts.
[10:18] Carlos: thanks maya, liam. bye.
---
